sections.h2: Which McIntosh County office answers a tax question?
sections.html:
Two buildings on North Way in Darien do most of the work. Assessors at number 601 appraise property and sign off on exemptions. The Tax Commissioner at number 1200, inside the county annex, mails the bills and receives payment. The commissioner's own page states that it sets neither value nor millage.

McIntosh County numbers worth keeping by the phone (source: county website and Tax Commissioner site)

Inside Darien there may be a second levy. The state says city taxes are billed by the city clerk unless the city and county agreed to one combined bill, so call Darien City Hall to find out.

sections.h2: What is it like to own a house in McIntosh County?
sections.html:
Marsh, tidal rivers and barrier islands define this county. The Census Bureau measures 574 square miles, and 150 of them are water. Darien started life as New Inverness in 1736, settled by Scottish Highlanders whom Oglethorpe had recruited, and the county separated from Liberty County in 1793. A British fort, Fort King George, went up in 1721. Federal troops burned Darien in June 1863.

Today the named places besides Darien are Crescent and Eulonia, both census-designated places, with Townsend and Valona unincorporated. Sapelo Island is the most familiar of the islands. Liberty, Glynn, Wayne and Long counties are the neighbors, and the county belongs to the Brunswick metro area.

  • Headcount: 11,989 in July 2025. That is 9.3 percent above the 2020 base of 10,970 yet short of the 14,333 recorded in 2010.
  • Homeownership: 80.0 percent, at a median value of $182,700 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Renters: median gross rent of $800.
  • Older residents: 28.2 percent are 65 and over, the highest share among the four places in this guide.
  • Pay and travel: households earn a median $50,273 and commute 37.5 minutes on average.
  • Space: 431.35 square miles of land hold 25.4 people per square mile.
  • Building: 106 permits went out in 2025.

sections.h2: How does flood zoning change a McIntosh County sale?
sections.html:
Low coastal plains leave parts of McIntosh County and Darien open to river, canal and hurricane flooding, and the county names St. Catherine's, Sapelo, Doboy and Altamaha Sounds as contributors. Because a buyer's lender may care about the flood zone, learn yours before listing.

The county and Darien both join the National Flood Insurance Program. Ordinary homeowners insurance generally leaves out flood, and a federally backed loan on a structure in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires a separate policy. Building and Zoning at 912-437-6603 looks up zones and base flood elevations and makes free site visits about flooding and drainage.

  • Under the county's 50 percent rule, repairs or renovations that raise a house's value by more than half require the lowest floor to be raised to at least base flood elevation when it sits below it.
  • Inside AE and VE zones, the underside of the lowest horizontal member must reach a foot above base flood elevation.
  • Suggested protection includes lifting electrical panels, heat pumps, water heaters and fuel tanks.

Call Building and Zoning before any pre-sale renovation, since the work itself can bring the elevation rules into play.

sections.h2: When are McIntosh County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Plan on November 15, or 60 days after the mailing date, whichever the bill uses. The Tax Commissioner's site warns that unpaid property can be levied on and eventually sold. State guidance describes the 60 days as running from the postmark and lets a county pick its own official date.

Returns are filed January 1 through April 1. Skip one and Georgia treats you as having returned the same property at the same value as the prior year. A dissatisfied owner may file a return naming a different fair market value, and that keeps appeal rights alive if the assessors then change the number again.

A mobile home located in the county on January 1 has an April 1 deadline for both the tax and the location permit. A late payer faces a 10 percent penalty, a citation to Magistrate Court or even sale of the home. To contest a mobile home value, an owner has 45 days to appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors.

Keep your mailing address current with the assessor or commissioner. Notices go to the last known address.

sections.h2: How have McIntosh County millage rates moved?
sections.html:
In September 2024 the county commission said it planned to collect 19.38 percent more than the rollback rate. The press release cited pay adjustments, a forecast 10 to 15 percent jump in employee health costs, inflation and the fact that millage had stayed flat for more than 15 years.

Because the rate exceeded rollback, state law called for three hearings, which the county held at Darien City Hall on September 26 and October 7, 2024.

For any later year, ask the County Commission Office for the adopted millage, and ask Darien City Hall for the city rate if the house is inside city limits.

sections.h2: What exemptions and appeal rights apply in McIntosh County?
sections.html:
File a homestead application at the Tax Assessor's Office. First-time owners should bring the warranty deed. The window to qualify for a year closes April 1, though Georgia accepts applications year round. Approval carries forward until you move, sell or switch exemption type. The county has local exemptions, and the bigger of local and state amounts is used.

  • Standard: $2,000 off the 40 percent assessed value, excluding bond levies.
  • Elderly school: up to $10,000 from age 62 with income of $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general: up to $4,000 from age 65 on the same income limit.
  • Floating: from age 62 with household income of $30,000 or less, replacing other state and county exemptions.
  • Deferral: from age 62 with gross income of $15,000 or less, running until ownership changes or deferred tax and interest hit 85 percent of market value.

Real property appeals go to the Board of Tax Assessors and need a postmark within 45 days of the notice mailing. Farmland can be assessed at 30 percent in place of 40, and conservation use taxes land at current use, each with a 10-year covenant.

sections.h2: What should a McIntosh County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Get the exact balance on each parcel from the Tax Commissioner, then ask the Assessor's Office if any value or exemption change is pending. Collect the flood zone and permit history before the listing goes live.

The state transfer tax is paid at deed recording. The revenue department prints it as $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents on each additional $100, owed by the seller unless the contract moves it. The Clerk of Superior Court answers exemption questions.

At the table, settle who pays this year's bill, whether a lender has been paying from escrow, and when your exemption comes off.

faqs.q: When is McIntosh County property tax due?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner's site gives November 15, or 60 days after mailing. Mobile homes are due April 1. Treat the date on your own bill as final.

faqs.q: Which office handles a disagreement over value in McIntosh County?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors at 601 North Way, 912-437-6663. The Tax Commissioner at 912-437-6627 bills and collects but does not change value.

faqs.q: Can flood rules affect a McIntosh County house sale?
faqs.a: They can. A federally backed loan on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires flood insurance, and the county's 50 percent rule may require a raised floor after major renovation.

faqs.q: What happens if a McIntosh County mobile home tax is not paid by April 1?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty applies, and the owner may be cited to McIntosh County Magistrate Court or lose the home to sale.

faqs.q: How do I apply for homestead exemption in McIntosh County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office and have the application in by April 1 to count for that year. New homeowners bring the warranty deed.
